annotations.summary: queue with pending tasks and no worker pool: {{ index $labels "workerPoolId" }}

model.expr:
# Alert: Pending Tasks Without a Worker Pool
# OWNER: relops
#
# This alert detects task queues that have pending tasks but no worker pool
# in worker-manager. No worker will ever claim these tasks. They wait until
# their deadline and then fail with deadline-exceeded.
#
# Example: enterprise-3/b-win2025-gpu (fxci-config#1427) and
# enterprise-{1,3}/b-linux-kvm. Each had 1-7 pending tasks, which is below
# the ">= 10" threshold of "queues with 1+ tasks and no running workers".
#
# How it works:
# 1. `sum by (provisionerId, workerType) (fxci_queue_pending_tasks) > 0`
#    - Selects queues with one or more pending tasks. No count threshold:
#      one stuck task is a problem when no pool exists.
#    - label_join builds workerPoolId = "<provisionerId>/<workerType>".
# 2. `max_over_time(fxci_worker_manager_desired_capacity[1h])`
#    - worker-manager emits this metric for each pool that it knows.
#      The 1h lookback ignores short scrape gaps.
# 3. `A unless on (workerPoolId) B`
#    - Returns only the queues that have no worker pool.
#
# Filters (provisioners that are not managed by worker-manager):
# - releng-hardware, proj-autophone (hardware workers)
# - scriptworker-k8s, scriptworker-prov-v1 (scriptworkers)
# - test-provisioner, built-in (Taskcluster internal)
#
# Fix: add the missing pool in mozilla-releng/fxci-config worker-pools.yml,
# or fix the taskQueueId of the task.
#
label_join(
  sum by (provisionerId, workerType)
    (fxci_queue_pending_tasks{provisionerId!~"releng-hardware|proj-autophone|scriptworker-k8s|scriptworker-prov-v1|test-provisioner|built-in"}) > 0,
  "workerPoolId", "/", "provisionerId", "workerType"
)
unless on (workerPoolId)
max by (workerPoolId)
  (max_over_time(fxci_worker_manager_desired_capacity[1h]))

title: queues with pending tasks and no worker pool
